name: ffmpeg
one_line: convert, cut and inspect audio and video
plain: `ffmpeg` reads media files (video, audio, images), changes them and writes new ones. In CTFs it is the tool for hidden things in media: extracting every frame of a video, pulling out the audio track, slowing a recording, or turning a sound into a picture of its spectrum.

The shape is `ffmpeg [input options] -i INPUT [output options] OUTPUT`. Options before `-i` apply to the input, options after apply to the output. `ffprobe` (same package) only inspects a file and changes nothing.
when: Pull the audio out of a video, or the frames out of a video.
Cut a short section to look at it closely.
Convert a strange format into one your player opens.
Inspect streams and metadata for hidden tracks or subtitles.
Speed up, slow down or reverse audio for a puzzle.

examples.title: Inspect first
examples.explain: Lists every stream: video, audio, subtitles, extra data tracks. A second audio stream or a data stream is often the hiding place.

examples.title: Extract the audio
examples.explain: -vn means no video; -acodec copy copies the audio without re-encoding (no quality loss).

examples.title: Convert audio to WAV
examples.explain: WAV is raw and easy for other tools (sox, Audacity, Python) to read.

examples.title: Every frame as a picture
examples.explain: Writes frame 1, 2, 3 ... as PNGs. Scroll through them or run exiftool/zsteg on them: a flag can sit on one frame.

examples.title: One frame per second
examples.explain: -vf is a video filter; fps=1 keeps one frame a second so you get far fewer pictures.

examples.title: Cut a section
examples.explain: -ss starts, -to ends; -c copy copies the streams unchanged, so it is instant.

examples.title: Slow audio down
examples.explain: atempo=0.5 plays at half speed without changing pitch. Good for Morse and fast spoken text.

examples.title: Reverse audio
examples.explain: A hidden message played backwards is a classic puzzle.

examples.title: Subtitles out
examples.explain: -map picks a stream: the first subtitle stream of input 0.

examples.title: Spectrogram picture
examples.explain: Draws the frequencies over time. Text or an image drawn into the spectrum shows up as a picture.

options.plain: Input file (use several times for several inputs).
Overwrite output without asking / never overwrite.
Start position (before -i seeks fast, after -i is exact).
Drop video / audio / subtitle / data streams.
Choose the codec; `copy` keeps the stream unchanged.
Choose exactly which streams go to the output (for example 0:a:1).
Filters that combine several inputs or outputs.
ffprobe options that print stream and container details.

mistakes: Putting -ss after -i on a long file and waiting minutes: put it before -i for a fast seek.
Re-encoding when you only needed a copy (use -c copy).
Forgetting that -y overwrites the output without asking.
Missing a second audio or data stream: always ffprobe first.
try: ffprobe a video you own and list its streams.
Extract one frame a second and look for text.
Slow a Morse recording to half speed and decode it by ear.
Make a spectrogram of a WAV and read it.
see_also: ffprobe(1), sox(1), exiftool(1), binwalk(1), steghide(1), Audacity, Sonic Visualiser.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
